questions.q: Which role sits at the top of Snowflake's built-in role hierarchy and encapsulates SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN?
options: A custom role you create yourself
questions.explain: ACCOUNTADMIN is the top-level role — it can do everything SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN can do, plus account-level tasks like billing, which is why it should be granted sparingly.

questions.q: Which built-in role is automatically granted to every user and role in a Snowflake account?
questions.explain: PUBLIC is the floor — every user and role has it whether or not it's explicitly granted.

questions.q: Which role is dedicated to creating and managing users and roles, and is inherited by SECURITYADMIN?
questions.explain: USERADMIN is the role that actually runs CREATE USER and CREATE ROLE in a well-run account, and SECURITYADMIN inherits it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which role typically ends up as the parent of custom roles like JUNIOR_DBA?
options: No role — custom roles are always independent
questions.explain: SYSADMIN creates and manages warehouses, databases and other objects, and custom roles are usually granted up to it so a system administrator can see and manage what those roles own.

questions.q: What two commands does this lesson use to slot a newly created custom role into the hierarchy?
options: GRANT ROLE ... TO USER, then GRANT ROLE ... TO ROLE
questions.explain: GRANT ROLE ... TO USER assigns the role to a person; GRANT ROLE ... TO ROLE (usually up to SYSADMIN) connects it into the hierarchy so it isn't an orphaned role.
